verses.1:1: Paul, called as an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother,
verses.1:2: to the church of God that is in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, along with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours:
verses.1:3: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:4: I give thanks to my God always concerning you for the grace of God that was given to you in Christ Jesus,
verses.1:5: that in every way you were enriched in Him, in all speech and all knowledge,
verses.1:6: just as the testimony of Christ was confirmed among you,
verses.1:7: so that you do not fall short in any gift, as you eagerly await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.1:8: who shall also confirm you until the end, blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:9: Faithful is God, through whom you were called into the fellowship of His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.1:10: Now I exhort you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be knit together in the same mind and in the same judgment.
verses.1:11: For it has been made known to me concerning you, my brethren, by those of Chloe's household, that there are contentions among you.
verses.1:12: Now I say this, that each one of you says, "I am of Paul," or "I of Apollos," or "I of Cephas," or "I of Christ."
verses.1:13: Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified on your behalf? Or were you baptized into the name of Paul?
verses.1:14: I give thanks that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
verses.1:15: lest anyone should say that you were baptized into my own name.
verses.1:16: Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized any other.
verses.1:17: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel—not in wisdom of speech, lest the cross of Christ be made void.
verses.1:18: For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, yet to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
verses.1:19: For it is written, "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the discernment of the discerning I will thwart."
verses.1:20: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Has God not made foolish the wisdom of the world?
verses.1:21: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through wisdom, God was well pleased through the foolishness of the proclamation to save those who believe.
verses.1:22: Indeed, Jews ask for signs and Greeks seek after wisdom,
verses.1:23: but we proclaim Christ crucified, to Jews a stumbling block and to Gentiles foolishness,
verses.1:24: yet to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
verses.1:25: For that which is foolish of God is wiser than men, and that which is weak of God is stronger than men.
verses.1:26: For consider your calling, brethren, that not many are wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many of noble birth.
verses.1:27: Rather, God chose the foolish things of the world in order to put to shame the wise, and God chose the weak things of the world in order to put to shame the things that are mighty,
verses.1:28: and the lowly things of the world and the things that are despised God chose, the things that are not, in order to bring to nothing the things that are,
verses.1:29: so that no flesh may boast in the presence of God.
verses.1:30: Yet from Him you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God—both righteousness and sanctification and redemption—
verses.1:31: so that, just as it is written, "Let him who boasts, boast in the Lord."
verses.2:1: And I, when I came to you, brethren, did not come with loftiness of speech or of wisdom, declaring to you the testimony of God.
verses.2:2: For I resolved to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.
verses.2:3: And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling,
verses.2:4: and my speech and my proclamation were not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,
verses.2:5: so that your faith might not rest in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
verses.2:6: Yet we do speak wisdom among the mature—a wisdom, however, not of this age, nor of the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing.
verses.2:7: Rather, we speak God's wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom, which God foreordained before the ages for our glory,
verses.2:8: which none of the rulers of this age has understood; for if they had understood it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
verses.2:9: But just as it is written, "Things which no eye has seen, and no ear has heard, and which have not entered the heart of man—the things God has prepared for those who love Him."
verses.2:10: For to us God revealed them through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God.
verses.2:11: For who among men knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man that is within him? In the same way also, no one has known the things of God except the Spirit of God.
verses.2:12: Now we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things freely bestowed upon us by God.
verses.2:13: These things we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom, but in those taught by the Spirit, interpreting spiritual things to the spiritual.
verses.2:14: But the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him; and he is not able to understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.
verses.2:15: Yet the spiritual man examines all things, while he himself is examined by no one.
verses.2:16: For "who has known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct Him?" Yet we possess the mind of Christ.
verses.3:1: And I, brethren, could not speak to you as to spiritual men, but as to men of flesh, as to infants in Christ.
verses.3:2: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able; indeed, even now you are still not able,
verses.3:3: for you are still carnal. For where jealousy and strife exist among you, are you not carnal, and walking as mere men?
verses.3:4: For when one says, "I am of Paul," and another, "I am of Apollos," are you not merely men?
verses.3:5: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? Servants through whom you believed, even as the Lord gave to each one.
verses.3:6: I planted, Apollos watered, but God was giving the growth.
verses.3:7: Therefore neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but only God who gives the growth.
verses.3:8: Now he who plants and he who waters are one, yet each shall receive his own reward according to his own labor.
verses.3:9: For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's cultivated field, you are God's building.
verses.3:10: According to the grace of God given to me, as a skilled master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds upon it. Yet let each one take heed how he builds upon it.
verses.3:11: For no one is able to lay any other foundation than that which is already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
verses.3:12: Now if anyone builds upon the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,
verses.3:13: each one's work shall become manifest; for the Day shall disclose it, because it is revealed in fire, and the fire itself shall test what sort each one's work is.
verses.3:14: If anyone's work that he has built upon it abides, he shall receive a reward.
verses.3:15: If anyone's work is burned up, he shall suffer loss; yet he himself shall be saved, though so as through fire.
verses.3:16: Do you not know that you are God's temple, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?
verses.3:17: If anyone destroys the temple of God, God shall destroy him; for the temple of God is holy, and that temple you are.
verses.3:18: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you thinks himself to be wise in this age, let him become foolish, so that he may become wise.
verses.3:19: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God; for it is written, "He catches the wise in their craftiness,"
verses.3:20: and again, "The Lord knows the reasonings of the wise, that they are futile."
verses.3:21: Therefore let no one boast in men. For all things belong to you:
verses.3:22: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come—all things are yours,
verses.3:23: and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
verses.4:1: In this manner let a man regard us: as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
verses.4:2: In this matter, moreover, it is required among stewards that one be found faithful.
verses.4:3: Yet to me it is a very small matter that I should be examined by you, or by any human tribunal; indeed, I do not even examine myself.
verses.4:4: For I am conscious of nothing against myself, yet I am not by this justified; rather, He who examines me is the Lord.
verses.4:5: Therefore do not judge anything before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both illuminate the secret things of darkness and make manifest the counsels of the hearts; and then praise shall come to each one from God.
verses.4:6: Now these things, brethren, I have applied figuratively to myself and Apollos for your sakes, that in us you may learn the rule, "Not beyond what is written," lest any one of you be puffed up on behalf of the one against the other.
verses.4:7: For who sets you apart from another? And what do you possess that you did not receive? Yet if indeed you received it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?
verses.4:8: Already you are filled! Already you have grown rich! Apart from us you have come to reign! And I wish indeed that you did reign, so that we also might reign together with you!
verses.4:9: For it seems to me that God has exhibited us, the apostles, last of all, like men sentenced to death; because we have become a spectacle to the world, both to angels and to men.
verses.4:10: We are fools for the sake of Christ, yet you are prudent in Christ; we are weak, yet you are strong; you are held in honor, yet we are in dishonor.
verses.4:11: Even to this present hour we both hunger and thirst, we are poorly clad, we are struck with blows, and we have no settled dwelling,
verses.4:12: and we toil, laboring with our own hands. When reviled, we bless; when persecuted, we endure;
verses.4:13: when slandered, we speak gently. We have become like the refuse of the world, the offscouring of all things, even until now.
verses.4:14: I am not writing these things to put you to shame, but to admonish you as my beloved children.
verses.4:15: For though you should have ten thousand guardians in Christ, yet you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
verses.4:16: I exhort you, therefore, become imitators of me.
verses.4:17: For this very reason I sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord; he will put you in remembrance of my ways in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every church.
verses.4:18: Now certain ones have become puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.
verses.4:19: Yet I will come to you quickly, if the Lord wills, and I shall discover not the speech of those who are puffed up, but the power;
verses.4:20: for the kingdom of God does not consist in speech, but in power.
verses.4:21: What do you desire? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of meekness?
verses.5:1: In fact, sexual immorality is reported among you, and of such a kind as is not even found among the Gentiles—that a man has his father's wife.
verses.5:2: And are you puffed up, and have you not rather mourned, so that he who has committed this deed might be removed from your midst?
verses.5:3: For I indeed, absent in body yet present in spirit, have already judged, as though present, him who has wrought this deed in such a way,
verses.5:4: in the name of our Lord Jesus, when you and my spirit are gathered together, with the power of our Lord Jesus,
verses.5:5: to hand such a one over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord.
verses.5:6: Your boasting is not fitting. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the entire lump of dough?
verses.5:7: Cleanse out the old leaven, that you may be a fresh lump, just as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover, has indeed been sacrificed.
verses.5:8: Therefore let us celebrate the festival, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
verses.5:9: I wrote to you in the letter not to associate with sexually immoral persons,
verses.5:10: not at all meaning the sexually immoral of this world, or the covetous and extortioners, or idolaters, since then you would be obliged to go out of the world.
verses.5:11: But now I write to you not to associate with anyone who bears the name of brother if he is sexually immoral, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner—not even to eat with such a man.
verses.5:12: For what is it to me to judge those who are outside? Do you not judge those who are inside,
verses.5:13: while God judges those who are outside? Expel the wicked man from among yourselves.
verses.6:1: Does any one of you, when he has a dispute against another, dare to go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?
verses.6:2: Or do you not know that the saints shall judge the world? And if the world is to be judged by you, are you unworthy to settle the smallest cases?
verses.6:3: Do you not know that we shall judge angels—how much more the affairs of this life?
verses.6:4: If, therefore, you have cases concerning the affairs of this life, do you seat as judges those who are of no account in the church?
verses.6:5: I speak this to your shame. Can it be that there is not even one wise man among you who will be able to decide between his brethren,
verses.6:6: but instead brother goes to law against brother, and that before unbelievers?
verses.6:7: In fact, it is already altogether a defeat for you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why do you not rather suffer wrong? Why do you not rather let yourselves be defrauded?
verses.6:8: Instead, you yourselves do wrong and defraud, and that to your own brethren.
verses.6:9: Or do you not know that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor men who lie with men,
verses.6:10: nor thieves, nor the covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners shall inherit the kingdom of God.
verses.6:11: And such were some of you; yet you were washed clean, yet you were sanctified, yet you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
verses.6:12: All things are lawful for me, yet not all things are profitable; all things are lawful for me, yet I will not be mastered by anything.
verses.6:13: Foods are for the stomach, and the stomach is for foods; yet God will bring both it and them to nothing. Now the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord is for the body;
verses.6:14: and God has both raised the Lord and shall also raise us up through His power.
verses.6:15: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I therefore take the members of Christ and make them into members of a harlot? May it never be!
verses.6:16: Or do you not know that he who unites himself to a harlot is one body with her? For He says, "The two shall become one flesh."
verses.6:17: Yet he who unites himself to the Lord is one spirit with Him.
verses.6:18: Flee from sexual immorality! Every sin that a man may commit is outside the body, yet he who practices sexual immorality sins against his own body.
verses.6:19: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? And you are not your own,
verses.6:20: for you were purchased with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body.
verses.7:1: Now concerning the matters about which you wrote: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.
verses.7:2: Yet because of cases of sexual immorality, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.
verses.7:3: Let the husband render to his wife what is due her, and likewise also the wife to her husband.
verses.7:4: The wife does not exercise authority over her own body, but the husband does; and likewise also the husband does not exercise authority over his own body, but the wife does.
verses.7:5: Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by mutual agreement for a season, that you may devote yourselves to prayer and be together again, lest Satan tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
verses.7:6: Now this I say by way of concession, not by way of command.
verses.7:7: Yet I wish that all men were even as I myself am; nevertheless, each one has his own gift from God, one in this manner and another in that.
verses.7:8: Now I say to the unmarried and to the widows, it is good for them if they abide even as I am;
verses.7:9: but if they do not exercise self-control, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.
verses.7:10: Now to the married I give charge, not I but the Lord, that a wife is not to separate from her husband—
verses.7:11: yet if indeed she separates, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and that a husband is not to divorce his wife.
verses.7:12: Now to the rest I say, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she consents to dwell with him, let him not divorce her.
verses.7:13: And a woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he consents to dwell with her, let her not divorce her husband.
verses.7:14: For the unbelieving husband has been sanctified in his wife, and the unbelieving wife has been sanctified in the brother; otherwise your children would be unclean, whereas now they are holy.
verses.7:15: Yet if the unbeliever separates, let him separate; the brother or the sister is not held in bondage in such cases, but God has called us in peace.
verses.7:16: For how do you know, wife, whether you shall save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you shall save your wife?
verses.7:17: Only, as the Lord has apportioned to each one, as God has called each one, so let him walk; and thus I ordain in all the churches.
verses.7:18: Was anyone called while circumcised? Let him not seek to undo his circumcision. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.
verses.7:19: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God.
verses.7:20: Each one, in the calling in which he was called, in that let him abide.
verses.7:21: Were you called as a bondservant? Do not let it trouble you; yet even if you are able to become free, rather make use of it.
verses.7:22: For the one who was called in the Lord as a bondservant is a freedman of the Lord; likewise the one who was called as a free man is a bondservant of Christ.
verses.7:23: You were bought with a price; do not become bondservants of men.
verses.7:24: Brethren, let each one abide with God in that condition in which he was called.
verses.7:25: Now concerning virgins, I have no command from the Lord, yet I offer my judgment as one shown mercy by the Lord to be trustworthy.
verses.7:26: I judge therefore that this is good because of the present distress—that it is good for a man to remain thus.
verses.7:27: Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Are you freed from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
verses.7:28: Yet even if you marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Nevertheless, such ones shall have affliction in the flesh, and I would spare you.
verses.7:29: Now this I declare, brethren: the time has been shortened, so that from now on even those who have wives should be as though they had none,
verses.7:30: and those who weep as though not weeping, and those who rejoice as though not rejoicing, and those who buy as though not possessing,
verses.7:31: and those who use the world as though not making full use of it; for the outward form of this world is passing away.
verses.7:32: Now I desire you to be free from care. The unmarried man cares for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;
verses.7:33: whereas the married man cares for the things of the world, how he may please his wife, and he is divided. And the unmarried woman, as well as the virgin
verses.7:34: who is unmarried, cares for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit; whereas the married woman cares for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
verses.7:35: Now this I say for your own benefit, not that I may cast a snare upon you, but for what is seemly and for devoted attendance upon the Lord without distraction.
verses.7:36: Yet if anyone judges that he is behaving improperly toward his virgin if she is past her prime, and thus it ought to be, let him do what he wills; he does not sin; let them marry.
verses.7:37: Yet he who stands steadfast in his heart, having no necessity, and has authority over his own will, and has determined this in his own heart, to keep his own virgin, shall do well.
verses.7:38: So then he who gives his own virgin in marriage does well, and he who does not give her in marriage shall do better.
verses.7:39: A wife is bound for as long a time as her husband lives; yet if her husband falls asleep, she is free to be married to whom she wishes, only in the Lord.
verses.7:40: Yet she is more blessed if she abides thus, according to my judgment; and I think that I also have the Spirit of God.
verses.8:1: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, yet love edifies.
verses.8:2: If anyone supposes that he has come to know anything, he has not yet known as he ought to know;
verses.8:3: yet if anyone loves God, this one has been known by Him.
verses.8:4: Concerning the eating therefore of things sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no God except one.
verses.8:5: For even if indeed there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, just as there are many gods and many lords,
verses.8:6: yet to us there is one God, the Father, from Whom are all things and we are for Him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through Whom are all things and we are through Him.
verses.8:7: Yet this knowledge is not in all; for some, through being accustomed until now to the idol, eat of it as something sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
verses.8:8: Now food will not commend us to God; neither if we eat do we abound, nor if we do not eat do we fall short.
verses.8:9: Yet take heed lest somehow this right of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.
verses.8:10: For if anyone sees you who have knowledge reclining at table in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, since he is weak, be emboldened to eat the things sacrificed to idols?
verses.8:11: For the weak one is perishing by your knowledge, the brother for whom Christ died.
verses.8:12: And thus, by sinning against the brethren and striking their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
verses.8:13: Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will by no means ever eat meat again, lest I cause my brother to stumble.
verses.9:1: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not beheld Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
verses.9:2: If to others I am not an apostle, yet surely I am to you; for you yourselves are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
verses.9:3: My defense to those who scrutinize me is this:
verses.9:4: Do we not have the right to eat and to drink?
verses.9:5: Do we not have the right to take along a sister as a wife, even as the rest of the apostles, the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas do?
verses.9:6: Or do only I and Barnabas lack the right to refrain from working?
verses.9:7: Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Or who shepherds a flock and does not partake of the milk of the flock?
verses.9:8: Do I speak these things merely as a man, or does the law not also say these very things?
verses.9:9: For in the law of Moses it is written, "You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing." Is it for oxen that God is concerned,
verses.9:10: or does He speak altogether for our sake? For on our account it was written, that he who plows ought to plow in hope, and he who threshes, in hope of partaking.
verses.9:11: If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it a great matter if we reap your material things?
verses.9:12: If others share in this right over you, do we not even more? Yet we did not make use of this right, but we bear all things, lest we place any obstacle before the gospel of Christ.
verses.9:13: Do you not know that those who perform the sacred duties eat from the temple, and those who attend at the altar share with the altar?
verses.9:14: In the same way also the Lord ordained that those who proclaim the gospel should live by the gospel.
verses.9:15: But I have made use of none of these things, nor have I written these things that it should be done thus in my case; for it would be better for me to die than—no one shall make my boast void!
verses.9:16: For if I proclaim the gospel, it is no ground for boasting to me, for necessity rests upon me; for woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!
verses.9:17: For if I do this of my own will, I have a reward; but if against my will, a stewardship has been entrusted to me.
verses.9:18: What then is my reward? That in proclaiming the gospel I may offer the gospel free of charge, so as not to make full use of my right in the gospel.
verses.9:19: For though I am free from all, I have made myself a bondservant to all, that I might win the more;
verses.9:20: and to the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might win Jews; to those under the law, as one under the law—though not myself under the law—that I might win those under the law;
verses.9:21: to those outside the law, as one outside the law—not being outside the law of God, but within the law of Christ—that I might win those outside the law;
verses.9:22: to the weak I became weak, that I might win the weak; to all I have become all things, that by every means I might save some.
verses.9:23: And I do all things for the sake of the gospel, that I may become a joint partaker of it.
verses.9:24: Do you not know that those who run in a race all run, yet one receives the prize? Run in such a manner that you may lay hold of it.
verses.9:25: And everyone who contends in the games exercises self-control in all things; they indeed do so to receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable one.
verses.9:26: Therefore I run in this way, not aimlessly; I box in this way, not as one beating the air;
verses.9:27: but I sternly discipline my body and bring it into subjection, lest perhaps, after preaching to others, I myself should become disqualified.
verses.10:1: For I do not wish you to be ignorant, brethren, that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea,
verses.10:2: and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
verses.10:3: and all ate the same spiritual food,
verses.10:4: and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they were drinking from a spiritual Rock that followed them, and the Rock was Christ.
verses.10:5: Yet with most of them God was not well pleased, for they were laid low in the wilderness.
verses.10:6: Now these things took place as examples for us, so that we should not lust after evil things, even as they also lusted.
verses.10:7: And do not become idolaters, as some of them did; even as it is written, "The people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play."
verses.10:8: Nor let us engage in sexual immorality, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in a single day;
verses.10:9: nor let us put the Lord to the test, as some of them tested Him, and were destroyed by the serpents;
verses.10:10: nor murmur, even as some of them murmured, and were destroyed by the destroyer.
verses.10:11: Now these things happened to them by way of example, and were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have arrived.
verses.10:12: Therefore let him who supposes he stands watch carefully, lest he fall.
verses.10:13: No temptation has seized you except what is common to mankind; yet God is faithful, who will not permit you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but together with the temptation He will also make the way out, so that you may be able to endure it.
verses.10:14: For this very reason, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
verses.10:15: I speak as to discerning people; judge for yourselves what I say.
verses.10:16: The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not fellowship in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not fellowship in the body of Christ?
verses.10:17: Since there is one loaf, we, the many, are one body; for all of us partake from the one loaf.
verses.10:18: Consider Israel according to the flesh: are those who eat the sacrifices not partners with the altar?
verses.10:19: What then do I say? That what is sacrificed to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?
verses.10:20: Rather, that what the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I do not wish you to become partners with demons.
verses.10:21: You are not able to drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you are not able to share in the table of the Lord and the table of demons.
verses.10:22: Or are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? Surely we are not stronger than He?
verses.10:23: All things are lawful, yet not all things are beneficial; all things are lawful, yet not all things edify.
verses.10:24: Let no one seek his own benefit, but that of the other.
verses.10:25: Eat whatever is sold in the meat market, making no inquiry on account of conscience;
verses.10:26: for to the Lord belongs the earth, and all its fullness.
verses.10:27: If one of the unbelievers invites you and you wish to go, eat whatever is set before you, making no inquiry on account of conscience.
verses.10:28: Yet if someone says to you, "This has been offered in sacrifice," do not eat it, on account of the one who informed you and for the sake of conscience;
verses.10:29: conscience, I mean, not your own, but that of the other. For why should my liberty be judged by another's conscience?
verses.10:30: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I reviled over that for which I give thanks?
verses.10:31: Therefore, whether you eat or whether you drink, or whatever you do, do all things to the glory of God.
verses.10:32: Give no cause for stumbling either to Jews or to Greeks or to the church of God,
verses.10:33: even as I also please everyone in all things, not seeking my own benefit, but that of the many, that they may be saved.
verses.11:1: Become imitators of me, even as I also am of Christ.
verses.11:2: Now I praise you because in all things you remember me and hold firmly to the traditions just as I delivered them to you.
verses.11:3: But I desire you to know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of a woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
verses.11:4: Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered puts his head to shame;
verses.11:5: but every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered puts her head to shame, for it is one and the same as having her head shaved.
verses.11:6: For if a woman does not cover herself, let her also be shorn; yet if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or to be shaved, let her cover herself.
verses.11:7: For a man truly ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; whereas the woman is the glory of man.
verses.11:8: For man is not from woman, but rather woman from man;
verses.11:9: and indeed man was not created for the sake of the woman, but woman for the sake of the man.
verses.11:10: For this reason the woman ought to have authority upon her head, because of the angels.
verses.11:11: Nevertheless, neither is woman apart from man, nor is man apart from woman, in the Lord;
verses.11:12: for just as the woman came from the man, so also does the man come through the woman; yet all things are from God.
verses.11:13: Judge among yourselves: is it fitting for a woman to pray to God uncovered?
verses.11:14: Does not even nature itself instruct you that if a man wears long hair, it is a dishonor to him,
verses.11:15: whereas if a woman wears long hair, it is a glory to her? For her long hair has been given to her in place of a covering.
verses.11:16: Yet if anyone is inclined to be contentious, we hold no such custom, nor do the churches of God.
verses.11:17: Now in giving this charge I do not commend you, because you assemble not for the better, but for the worse.
verses.11:18: For in the first place, when you come together as a church, I hear that divisions exist among you, and in part I believe it.
verses.11:19: For there must indeed be factions among you, in order that those who are approved may also become manifest among you.
verses.11:20: When you assemble together in one place, therefore, it is not the Lord's Supper that you eat,
verses.11:21: for in the meal each one takes his own supper beforehand, and one remains hungry while another is drunk.
verses.11:22: What! Do you not have houses in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and put to shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I commend you? In this I do not commend you.
verses.11:23: For I myself received from the Lord what I also handed down to you, that the Lord Jesus, on the night in which He was betrayed, took bread,
verses.11:24: and after He had given thanks, He broke it and said, "This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me."
verses.11:25: In like manner He also took the cup after supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me."
verses.11:26: For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the death of the Lord until He comes.
verses.11:27: Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner shall be guilty concerning the body and the blood of the Lord.
verses.11:28: But let a man test himself, and so let him eat from the bread and drink from the cup;
verses.11:29: for whoever eats and drinks, without discerning the body, eats and drinks judgment upon himself.
verses.11:30: For this reason many among you are weak and ill, and not a few sleep.
verses.11:31: But if we discerned ourselves rightly, we would not be judged;
verses.11:32: but when we are judged by the Lord, we are chastened, lest we be condemned together with the world.
verses.11:33: Therefore, my brethren, when you assemble to eat, wait for one another.
verses.11:34: If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, lest you assemble for judgment. As for the rest, I shall set them in order when I come.
verses.12:1: Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I do not wish you to be ignorant.
verses.12:2: You know that when you were Gentiles, you were carried off toward mute idols, in whatever way you were led.
verses.12:3: Therefore I make it known to you that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, "Accursed is Jesus," nor is anyone able to say, "Jesus is Lord," except by the Holy Spirit.
verses.12:4: Now there are diversities of gifts, yet the same Spirit;
verses.12:5: and there are diversities of ministries, and the same Lord;
verses.12:6: and there are diversities of workings, yet it is the same God who works all things in all.
verses.12:7: Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common profit.
verses.12:8: for to one through the Spirit is given a word of wisdom, and to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,
verses.12:9: to another faith by the same Spirit, and to another gifts of healings by the one Spirit,
verses.12:10: and to another workings of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discernings of spirits, to another various kinds of tongues, and to another the interpretation of tongues;
verses.12:11: yet one and the same Spirit works all these things, apportioning to each one individually just as He wills.
verses.12:12: For just as the body is one and possesses many members, and all the members of the body, though being many, are one body, so also is Christ;
verses.12:13: for indeed in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body—whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free—and all were made to drink of one Spirit.
verses.12:14: For truly the body is not one member, but many.
verses.12:15: If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I am not part of the body," is it therefore not part of the body?
verses.12:16: And if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I am not part of the body," it is not on that account any less part of the body;
verses.12:17: If the entire body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
verses.12:18: But as it is, God placed the members, every single one of them, in the body just as He willed.
verses.12:19: And if all were a single member, where would the body be?
verses.12:20: As it is, however, there are many members, yet one body.
verses.12:21: And the eye is unable to say to the hand, "I have no need of you," nor again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you";
verses.12:22: on the contrary, much rather, those members of the body that appear to be weaker are indispensable,
verses.12:23: and those parts of the body that we consider less honorable, upon these we bestow more abundant honor; and our unseemly parts receive greater modesty,
verses.12:24: whereas our presentable parts have no such need. Rather, God has blended the body together, giving more abundant honor to the part that lacks it,
verses.12:25: lest there be any schism in the body, but rather that the members should show equal care for one another.
verses.12:26: And whether one member suffers, all the members suffer together with it; or a member is honored, all the members rejoice together with it.
verses.12:27: Now you are Christ's body, and each of you a member in particular.
verses.12:28: And God has appointed some in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healings, deeds of help, administrations, kinds of tongues.
verses.12:29: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work mighty deeds?
verses.12:30: Do all possess gifts of healings? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
verses.12:31: Yet earnestly desire the greater gifts. And still I show you a surpassingly excellent way.
verses.13:1: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, yet do not have love, I have become resounding bronze or a clashing cymbal.
verses.13:2: And if I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains, yet do not have love, I am nothing.
verses.13:3: And if I distribute all my possessions, and if I deliver up my body that I may boast, yet do not have love, I profit nothing.
verses.13:4: Love is longsuffering, love is kind; love is not envious, does not boast, is not puffed up,
verses.13:5: it does not behave improperly, does not seek what is its own, is not provoked to anger, does not keep account of wrong;
verses.13:6: it does not rejoice over unrighteousness, but rejoices together with the truth;
verses.13:7: it bears all things, trusts all things, hopes for all things, steadfastly endures all things.
verses.13:8: Love shall never fail. Yet whether there are prophecies, they shall be brought to an end; whether there are tongues, they shall cease; whether there is knowledge, it shall be brought to an end.
verses.13:9: For in part we know, and in part we prophesy;
verses.13:10: but when that which is perfect comes, that which is in part shall be brought to an end.
verses.13:11: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I thought as a child, I reasoned as a child; when I became a man, I put away the ways of a child.
verses.13:12: For now we see through a mirror obscurely, yet then face to face; now I know in part, yet then I shall know fully, even as I also have been fully known.
verses.13:13: Yet now faith, hope, and love abide—these three; and the greatest of these is love.
verses.14:1: Pursue love, and earnestly desire the spiritual gifts, yet especially that you may prophesy.
verses.14:2: For the one who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God, for no one understands; rather, in spirit he utters mysteries.
verses.14:3: Yet the one who prophesies speaks to men edification, exhortation, and consolation.
verses.14:4: The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, whereas the one who prophesies edifies the church.
verses.14:5: Now I desire that you all speak in tongues, yet even more that you prophesy; and greater is the one who prophesies than the one who speaks in tongues, unless indeed he interprets, that the church may receive edification.
verses.14:6: Now then, brethren, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what benefit shall I bring you unless I speak to you either by revelation, or by knowledge, or by prophecy, or by instruction?
verses.14:7: Even so, lifeless things that produce a sound, whether flute or harp—if they do not make a distinction in the tones, how shall it be known what is played on the flute or on the harp?
verses.14:8: For indeed, if a trumpet gives an indistinct call, who shall prepare himself for battle?
verses.14:9: So likewise you—if with the tongue you do not utter intelligible speech, how will what is spoken be known? For you will be speaking into the air.
verses.14:10: There are, it may be, so many kinds of languages in the world, and not one is without meaning;
verses.14:11: therefore, if I do not know the meaning of the language, I shall be a foreigner to the one who speaks, and the one who speaks shall be a foreigner to me.
verses.14:12: So also with you: since you are zealous for spiritual gifts, seek to abound in them for the edification of the church.
verses.14:13: Therefore, let whoever speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret.
verses.14:14: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, yet my mind is unfruitful.
verses.14:15: What then shall I do? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the mind; I will sing praise with the spirit, and I will also sing praise with the mind.
verses.14:16: Otherwise, if you bless in spirit, how will the one who occupies the place of the uninstructed say the "Amen" at your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
verses.14:17: For you indeed give thanks well, yet the other person is not edified.
verses.14:18: I give thanks to God that I speak in tongues more than you all;
verses.14:19: yet in the church I would rather speak five words with my mind, in order that I may also instruct others, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
verses.14:20: Brethren, do not become children in your thinking; rather, in malice be infants, yet in your thinking be mature.
verses.14:21: In the Law it is written: "By people of foreign tongues and by the lips of others I will speak to this people, and even so they will not listen to Me," says the Lord.
verses.14:22: So then, tongues serve as a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers; whereas prophecy is not for unbelievers, but for believers.
verses.14:23: If therefore the whole church gathers together in one place and all speak in tongues, and uninstructed persons or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your minds?
verses.14:24: Yet if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or an uninstructed person enters, he is convicted by all, he is called to account by all;
verses.14:25: the secrets of his heart are made manifest; and so, falling upon his face, he will worship God, declaring, "Truly God is among you."
verses.14:26: What then is to be done, brethren? Whenever you assemble together, each one has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification.
verses.14:27: If anyone speaks in a tongue, let it be by two, or at the most three, and each in turn, and let one interpret;
verses.14:28: but if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the church, and let him speak to himself and to God.
verses.14:29: And let two or three prophets speak, and let the others weigh what is spoken;
verses.14:30: yet if something is revealed to another who is seated, let the first keep silent.
verses.14:31: For you can all prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all may be encouraged
verses.14:32: (and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets,
verses.14:33: for God is not a God of disorder, but of peace), as in all the churches of the saints.
verses.14:34: Let the women keep silent in the churches, for they are not permitted to speak; rather, let them be in subjection, even as the Law also says.
verses.14:35: And if they desire to learn anything, let them inquire of their own husbands at home; for it is shameful for a woman to speak in the church.
verses.14:36: Or did the word of God go forth from you, or has it reached you alone?
verses.14:37: If anyone considers himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things I write to you are of the Lord—a commandment.
verses.14:38: Yet if anyone is ignorant, let him remain ignorant.
verses.14:39: Therefore, my brethren, earnestly desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues;
verses.14:40: yet let all things be done fittingly and in good order.
verses.15:1: Now I make known to you, brethren, the gospel which I proclaimed to you, which you also received, in which you also stand,
verses.15:2: through which you are also being saved, if you hold fast the word that I proclaimed to you—unless indeed you believed in vain.
verses.15:3: For I handed down to you as of foremost importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
verses.15:4: and that He was buried, and that He has been raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
verses.15:5: and that He appeared to Cephas, and then to the twelve;
verses.15:6: after that He appeared to over five hundred brethren at one time, the greater part of whom remain to this present time, though some have fallen asleep;
verses.15:7: afterward He appeared to James, and then to all the apostles;
verses.15:8: and last of all, as to an untimely birth, He appeared to me also.
verses.15:9: For I am the least of the apostles, unfit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
verses.15:10: Yet by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace toward me did not prove in vain; on the contrary, I labored more abundantly than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God with me.
verses.15:11: Whether then it is I or they, thus we preach, and thus you believed.
verses.15:12: Now if it is preached of Christ that He has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
verses.15:13: Yet if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised;
verses.15:14: and if Christ has not been raised, then empty is our preaching, and empty also is your faith;
verses.15:15: moreover, we are also found to be false witnesses of God, because we bore witness concerning God that He raised up Christ—whom He did not raise, if indeed the dead are not raised.
verses.15:16: For if the dead are not raised, neither has Christ been raised;
verses.15:17: and if Christ has not been raised, your faith is fruitless; you are still in your sins.
verses.15:18: Then indeed those who fell asleep in Christ have perished.
verses.15:19: If in this life alone we have placed our hope in Christ, we are more to be pitied than all men.
verses.15:20: Yet now Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
verses.15:21: For since death came through a man, through a Man also comes the resurrection of the dead;
verses.15:22: for just as in Adam all die, so also in Christ shall all be made alive.
verses.15:23: Yet each one in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, and afterward those who belong to Christ at His coming;
verses.15:24: then comes the end, when He delivers up the kingdom to God the Father, when He has abolished every rule and every authority and power.
verses.15:25: For He must reign until He has placed all enemies beneath His feet.
verses.15:26: The last enemy to be abolished is death.
verses.15:27: For "He has subjected all things beneath His feet." Yet when it says, "All things have been subjected," it is evident that this is apart from the One who subjected all things to Him.
verses.15:28: And when all things have been subjected to Him, then the Son Himself shall also be subjected to the One who subjected all things to Him, that God may be all in all.
verses.15:29: Otherwise, what will those do who are baptized on behalf of the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why then are they baptized on their behalf?
verses.15:30: And why do we also stand in peril every hour?
verses.15:31: Daily I die—I affirm it by the boasting in you, brethren, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.15:32: If from human motives I fought with wild beasts in Ephesus, what gain is it to me? If the dead are not raised, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
verses.15:33: Do not be led astray: "Evil associations corrupt good character."
verses.15:34: Awake to soberness as is right, and do not go on sinning; for some have no knowledge of God. To your shame I speak this.
verses.15:35: Yet someone will say, "How are the dead raised, and with what sort of body do they come?"
verses.15:36: Foolish one! That which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies;
verses.15:37: and what you sow, you do not sow the body that shall be, but a bare kernel—perhaps of wheat, or of some other seed;
verses.15:38: yet God gives it a body just as He has willed, and to each of the seeds its own body.
verses.15:39: Not all flesh is the same flesh, but there is one kind of men, another flesh of beasts, another flesh of birds, and another of fish.
verses.15:40: There are both heavenly bodies and earthly bodies; yet one is the glory of the heavenly, and another is that of the earthly.
verses.15:41: One is the glory of the sun, and another the glory of the moon, and another the glory of the stars; for star differs from star in glory.
verses.15:42: Thus it is also with the resurrection of the dead: it is sown in corruption, and it is raised in incorruption;
verses.15:43: it is sown in dishonor, and it is raised in glory; it is sown in weakness, and it is raised in power;
verses.15:44: it is sown a natural body, and it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is a spiritual body as well.
verses.15:45: Thus also it stands written: "The first man, Adam, became a living soul"; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
verses.15:46: Yet the spiritual is not first, but rather the natural, and afterward the spiritual.
verses.15:47: The first man is from the earth, made of dust; the second Man is from heaven.
verses.15:48: As is the one made of dust, so also are those who are made of dust; and as is the heavenly One, so also are those who are heavenly.
verses.15:49: And just as we have borne the image of the one made of dust, let us also bear the image of the heavenly One.
verses.15:50: Now this I declare, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, neither does corruption inherit incorruption.
verses.15:51: Behold, I speak a mystery to you: we shall not all fall asleep, yet all of us shall be changed,
verses.15:52: in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet; for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we ourselves shall be changed.
verses.15:53: For this which is corruptible must clothe itself with incorruption, and this which is mortal must clothe itself with immortality.
verses.15:54: And when this which is corruptible has clothed itself with incorruption, and this which is mortal has clothed itself with immortality, then shall come to pass the word that stands written: "Death has been swallowed up in victory."
verses.15:55: "Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?"
verses.15:56: Now the sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law;
verses.15:57: yet thanks be to God, who grants us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.15:58: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be steadfast, unshakable, abounding in the work of the Lord at all times, knowing that your toil is not in vain in the Lord.
verses.16:1: Now concerning the collection for the saints, just as I instructed the churches of Galatia, so you must do also.
verses.16:2: On the first day of every week, let each one of you set something aside by himself, storing up according as he may prosper, lest collections be made when I come.
verses.16:3: And when I arrive, whomever you approve by letters, these I will send to carry your gracious gift to Jerusalem;
verses.16:4: and if it is fitting for me to go as well, they shall travel with me.
verses.16:5: Now I will come to you once I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia,
verses.16:6: and perhaps I shall remain with you, or even pass the winter, so that you may send me on my way wherever I may go.
verses.16:7: For I do not wish to see you now in passing, for I hope to abide with you for some time, if the Lord permits.
verses.16:8: But I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost;
verses.16:9: for a wide and effective door stands open to me, and there are many adversaries.
verses.16:10: Now if Timothy comes, see to it that he is with you without fear, for he performs the work of the Lord, just as I do.
verses.16:11: Let no one therefore despise him. Rather, send him on his way in peace, so that he may come to me, for I am awaiting him with the brethren.
verses.16:12: Now concerning Apollos our brother, I urged him greatly to come to you with the brethren; yet it was not at all his will to come now, but he will come when he has an opportunity.
verses.16:13: Keep watch, stand steadfast in the faith, be valiant, be strong.
verses.16:14: Let everything you do be done in love.
verses.16:15: Now I exhort you, brethren—you know the household of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have dedicated themselves to the service of the saints—
verses.16:16: that you also submit yourselves to such ones, and to every fellow worker and laborer.
verses.16:17: Now I rejoice over the arrival of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, for these men have made up for what was lacking on your part,
verses.16:18: for they refreshed both my spirit and yours. Therefore recognize such men.
verses.16:19: The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the church in their house.
verses.16:20: All the brethren send you their greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
verses.16:21: This greeting is by my own hand—Paul's.
verses.16:22: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be accursed. Maranatha.
verses.16:23: May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
verses.16:24: My love is with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

notes.1:2: The closing phrase "both theirs and ours" (Greek auton kai hemon) can grammatically modify either "every place" or "our Lord Jesus Christ," preserving the breadth of Christian fellowship across all congregations.
notes.1:14: The Greek critical text reads simply "I give thanks" without "to God," and in 1:15 reads the second-person plural "that you were baptized" rather than the later variant "that I baptized."
notes.1:23: The Greek text reads "to Gentiles" (ethnesin) rather than "to Greeks" (Hellesin), contrasting Israel with the nations as a whole.
notes.2:1: The Greek text reads "the testimony of God" (to martyrion tou theou); an ancient manuscript variant reads "the mystery of God" (to mysterion tou theou).
notes.2:13: The Greek participial clause (pneumatikois pneumatika synkrinontes) is syntactically open and may also be rendered "combining spiritual truths with spiritual words" or "comparing spiritual things with spiritual."
notes.2:14: "The natural man" translates Greek psychikos anthropos (literally "soulish man"), denoting a person who lives solely by unrenewed human faculties without the Spirit of God.
notes.3:1: Paul here uses sarkinois ("of flesh," pointing to immaturity), shifting in 3:3 to sarkikoi ("carnal," pointing to fleshly behavior marked by jealousy and strife).
notes.3:5: Paul deliberately employs the neuter pronoun "What" (ti) rather than "Who," emphasizing the instrumental role of apostles as servants rather than rival patrons.
notes.3:9: "God's fellow workers" (theou synergoi) can mean either fellow laborers who belong to God or co-workers who labor together with God.
notes.3:13: "The Day" refers to the final Day of the Lord, when the true quality of each builder's work will be disclosed and tested.
notes.4:3: The Greek phrase rendered "human tribunal" is literally "human day," referring to a day appointed for human court proceedings in contrast to the coming day of the Lord.
notes.4:6: The Saints Greek text preserves the elliptical maxim "Not beyond what is written" without the explanatory verb "to think" added in later manuscripts.
notes.4:15: The Greek word paidagogos ("guardian") denoted a household attendant responsible for supervising a child's conduct, contrasted here with the unique bond of a spiritual father.
notes.5:4: The Saints Greek text reads "our Lord Jesus" in both clauses (without "Christ"), and in 5:5 reads "the day of the Lord" (without "Jesus").
notes.5:7: The Saints Greek text reads simply "has been sacrificed," without the explanatory phrase "for us" found in later manuscripts.
notes.5:13: The closing command echoes the recurring formula of Deuteronomy (for example, Deut 17:7 and 21:21 LXX) instructing Israel to remove evil from its midst.
notes.6:4: Following the punctuation of the Greek text, the verb is rendered as a question ("do you seat...?"), though some interpreters read it as an ironic imperative ("appoint them!").
notes.6:9: The Greek uses two distinct terms: malakoi ("the effeminate," referring in antiquity to the passive partner in male same-sex acts) and arsenokoitai ("men who lie with men," a compound reflecting Lev 18:22 and 20:13 LXX).
notes.6:12: The repeated assertion "All things are lawful for me" (along with "Foods are for the stomach, and the stomach is for foods" in 6:13) is widely understood as echoing slogans circulating in Corinth that Paul qualifies and corrects.
notes.6:20: The Saints Greek text ends at "in your body," omitting the later manuscript addition "and in your spirit, which are God's."
notes.7:1: The statement 'it is good for a man not to touch a woman' is widely taken as a slogan quoted from the Corinthians' letter rather than Paul's own maxim, though the Greek text has no quotation marks.
notes.7:21: The terse imperative 'rather make use of it' (Greek mallon chresai) supplies no explicit object and is debated: most interpreters understand it as availing oneself of the opportunity for freedom, while some take it as making use of one's present station in Christ.
notes.7:33: Following the critical Greek text, 'and he is divided' concludes verse 33, while 'who is unmarried' at the opening of verse 34 modifies 'the virgin' at the close of verse 33.
notes.7:36: The expression 'his virgin' in verses 36-38 is interpreted either as a father's virgin daughter (especially with 'gives in marriage' in v. 38) or as a betrothed man's fiancée; the literal rendering retains the Greek ambiguity.
notes.8:1: The claim 'we all have knowledge' (and similarly the monotheistic statements in v. 4) may echo a Corinthian slogan that Paul qualifies by setting love above mere knowledge.
notes.8:7: The critical Greek text reads 'through being accustomed to' (synetheia) rather than 'with consciousness of' (syneidesei), pointing to the lingering pull of former idolatrous habit.
notes.8:10: The verb 'be emboldened' translates Greek oikodomethesetai (literally 'be built up'), echoing 'love edifies' in verse 1 with sharp irony.
notes.9:1: The Greek critical text places "Am I not free?" before "Am I not an apostle?", reversing the order found in later Byzantine manuscripts.
notes.9:5: Literally "a sister, a wife," referring to a believing Christian wife.
notes.9:15: The Greek sentence breaks off abruptly (anacoluthon) after "than," reflecting Paul's strong emotion as he refuses even to state the alternative to death.
notes.9:20: The Greek critical text includes the clarifying parenthetical clause "though not myself under the law," which is absent from later Byzantine manuscripts.
notes.10:8: Paul specifies twenty-three thousand falling in a single day, whereas Numbers 25:9 records twenty-four thousand as the total toll of the plague.
notes.10:9: This Greek text reads "the Lord" (ton Kyrion), whereas other early manuscripts read "Christ" (ton Christon).
notes.10:20: This Greek text explicitly includes "the Gentiles" as the subject of the sacrifices offered to demons.
notes.10:28: The Greek uses hierothyton ("offered in sacrifice," the neutral term a pagan host would use) rather than eidolothyton ("offered to idols"), and omits the repetition of Psalm 24:1 found at the end of the verse in later manuscripts.
notes.11:3: Greek aner and gyne can mean either "man/woman" or "husband/wife," and kephale ("head") is debated as signifying authority, source, or prominence.
notes.11:10: Greek exousian literally means "authority," often understood either as a sign of authority on the woman's head or as her own authority to pray and prophesy; the meaning of "because of the angels" is also debated.
notes.11:15: Greek anti peribolaiou can be understood either as "in place of a covering" (substitutional) or "as a covering" (functional equivalent).
notes.11:24: The critical Greek text reads simply "which is for you," without the later Byzantine additions "Take, eat" and "broken" found in some manuscripts.
notes.11:29: The critical Greek text omits "in an unworthy manner" and "of the Lord," leaving "the body" open to referring to Christ's sacrificed body, the church as His body, or both.
notes.12:1: Greek ton pneumatikon may be neuter ("spiritual gifts" or "spiritual matters") or masculine ("spiritual persons").
notes.12:2: The Greek syntax is abrupt (anacoluthon), combining "when you were Gentiles" with the participle "being carried off" to depict the compelling pull of pagan idolatry.
notes.12:13: The critical Greek text reads "made to drink of one Spirit" without the preposition "into" found in later manuscripts.
notes.12:31: The critical Greek text reads ta meizona ("the greater" gifts) rather than the later variant ta kreittona ("the best" gifts), and zeloute may be taken either as an imperative ("earnestly desire") or an indicative ("you are earnestly desiring").
notes.13:3: The critical Greek text reads 'that I may boast' (kauchesomai) rather than the later textual variant 'to be burned' (kauthesomai).
notes.13:4: The Greek text repeats 'love' three times at the opening of this verse ('Love is longsuffering, love is kind; love is not envious'), underscoring its centrality.
notes.13:12: Greek 'en ainigmati' literally means 'in a riddle' or 'in an obscure reflection,' alluding to the dim image cast by ancient polished metal mirrors.
notes.14:2: Greek 'pneumati' ('in spirit') appears without the article and may refer either to the speaker's own spirit (compare verses 14-15) or to the Holy Spirit.
notes.14:12: Literally 'zealous for spirits,' referring contextually to manifestations or gifts of the Spirit.
notes.14:33: Following the punctuation of the Greek text, 'as in all the churches of the saints' concludes verses 31-33; some editions attach this clause to the beginning of verse 34.
notes.14:38: The Greek text reads the active imperative 'let him remain ignorant' (agnoeito); an ancient textual variant reads the passive 'he is not recognized' (agnoeitai).
notes.15:29: The precise practice behind being baptized on behalf of the dead is widely debated among interpreters, ranging from proxy baptism for departed believers to baptism undertaken in hope of reunion with deceased Christians. In the second question, the Greek critical text reads "on their behalf" rather than repeating "for the dead."
notes.15:47: The Greek critical text reads simply "the second Man is from heaven," without the later Byzantine addition "the Lord."
notes.15:49: The Greek text reads the hortatory subjunctive ("let us also bear"), attested by the majority of early manuscripts, while other witnesses read the future indicative ("we shall also bear").
notes.15:55: Following the earliest Greek manuscripts, this verse places "victory" before "sting" and addresses "Death" in both clauses rather than "Hades" in the second.
notes.16:3: The Greek phrase "by letters" may modify either "approve" (as punctuated in the Greek text) or "send," yielding "those whom you approve I will send with letters."
notes.16:12: Literally "there was not at all a will," which is ambiguous in Greek and may refer either to Apollos's own inclination or to the will of God.
notes.16:13: The Greek verb rendered "be valiant" literally means "act like men," an idiom for displaying courage and steadfast resolve.
notes.16:22: "Maranatha" transliterates an Aramaic expression left untranslated in the Greek; divided as in this text, it is a prayer meaning "Our Lord, come!" (if divided differently, it can mean "Our Lord has come").
